dedupe_keys.name: vittel nestle waters france payments for ecosystem services to protect a mineral water aquifer iied 2006

description: This case study analyses the payments for ecosystem services programme that Vittel, the mineral water brand of Nestlé Waters, set up in north-eastern France to stop nitrate contamination of its aquifer from intensifying agriculture. Danièle Perrot-Maître wrote it as IIED Project Paper No. 3 in September 2006, with help from Nestlé Waters staff and IUCN. Vittel financed farmers in the catchment to change farming practices and technology, after identifying alternatives, understanding farmers and the science, and a ten-year process of participatory research and negotiation that turned conflict into partnership. The paper concludes that keeping farmers' income level and paying for all changes mattered, but trust built through a locally based intermediary led by a champion was the main reason for success, and asks whether it is a perfect PES case. Coverage is the Vittel catchment. Format and access: a 24-page PDF. Licence: not stated; free. Caveats: it is a qualitative account by one author, and costs are given only in outline. It shows catchment protection as green infrastructure for water supply. Related catalogue records are the Rio Camboriú watershed ROI study and the Sebago watershed economic case.

outcomes: Paying farmers to change practices and technology removed the nitrate risk to the aquifer; success rested less on money than on trust built through a local intermediary institution, a decade of participatory research and keeping farmers' incomes whole.
